questions.stem: Radioactivity was first discovered by:
questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 accidentally while studying phosphorescence of uranium salts. Marie Curie and Pierre Curie later coined the term 'radioactivity' and discovered polonium and radium.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Alpha particles (α) are identical to:
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are helium-4 nuclei — 2 protons and 2 neutrons, charge +2. They have low penetrating power (stopped by a sheet of paper) but high ionising power.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Beta (β) particles are fast-moving:
questions.explanation: β⁻ particles are fast electrons; β⁺ particles are positrons. Beta emission occurs when a neutron decays to a proton + electron (β⁻) or proton decays to neutron + positron (β⁺).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Gamma rays (γ) are:
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy, short-wavelength electromagnetic radiation (like very energetic X-rays) emitted from excited nuclei. They have the highest penetrating power — require several cm of lead or metres of concrete to attenuate.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Nuclear fission is the process in which a heavy nucleus:

options.option_text: Absorbs a neutron and releases energy as light
Splits into two smaller nuclei releasing a large amount of energy
Combines with another nucleus to form a heavier element

questions.explanation: Nuclear fission: a heavy nucleus (e.g., ²³⁵U) absorbs a slow neutron and splits into two medium-sized nuclei + 2–3 neutrons + enormous energy (Einstein's E=mc²). Basis of nuclear reactors and atom bombs.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Nuclear fusion involves:

options.option_text: Combining light nuclei (e.g., hydrogen) to form a heavier nucleus with release of huge energy

questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion: two light nuclei (e.g., H-2 + H-3) combine to form a heavier nucleus (He-4) + neutron + enormous energy. Basis of the sun's energy and hydrogen bombs. Requires extremely high temperature (~100 million K).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The radioactive isotope used in carbon dating is:
questions.explanation: Carbon-14 (¹⁴C, radiocarbon) is a radioactive isotope (t½ ≈ 5,730 years) formed in the atmosphere and absorbed by living organisms. After death, ¹⁴C decays at a known rate — used to date organic material up to ~50,000 years old.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The half-life of a radioactive element is the time taken for:

options.option_text: Half of the atoms in a sample to decay
The radiation to halve in frequency

questions.explanation: Half-life (t½): time for half the radioactive atoms in a sample to undergo decay. After n half-lives, fraction remaining = (½)ⁿ. Each isotope has a characteristic, constant half-life.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: In a nuclear reactor, the chain reaction is controlled using:
questions.explanation: Control rods (cadmium or boron) absorb excess neutrons, slowing or stopping the chain reaction. The moderator (heavy water or graphite) slows neutrons; the coolant removes heat. Control rods regulate reactor power.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which of the following is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors to slow down fast neutrons?
questions.explanation: Moderators slow fast neutrons to thermal (slow) velocities needed for efficient ²³⁵U fission. Common moderators: heavy water (D₂O), light water (H₂O), graphite. Heavy water is used in India's CANDU-type PHWR reactors.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The radiation used in cancer treatment (radiotherapy) to destroy tumour cells is:
questions.explanation: Gamma radiation from Cobalt-60 (Co-60) or X-rays from linear accelerators is used in external beam radiotherapy to destroy cancer cells. High-energy gamma rays penetrate deep tissues.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: When uranium-238 emits an alpha particle, the resulting nucleus is:
questions.explanation: Alpha emission: atomic number decreases by 2, mass number by 4. U-238 (Z=92, A=238) → Th-234 (Z=90, A=234) + α (Z=2, A=4).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Iodine-131, a radioactive isotope used in the treatment of thyroid cancer, has a half-life of about 8 days. Starting with 160 g, how much remains after 24 days?
questions.explanation: 24 days = 3 half-lives (24/8 = 3). Remaining = 160 × (½)³ = 160/8 = 20 g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which country conducted the first nuclear weapon test on 16 July 1945?
questions.explanation: The USA conducted the Trinity test (Manhattan Project) on 16 July 1945 at Alamogordo, New Mexico — the world's first nuclear weapon test. The bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki followed on 6 and 9 August 1945.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: India's first nuclear test, codenamed 'Smiling Buddha', was conducted in:
questions.explanation: India's first nuclear test (codenamed 'Smiling Buddha' or Pokhran-I) was conducted on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan. Pokhran-II ('Operation Shakti') followed in May 1998.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The phenomenon where certain elements spontaneously emit radiation without any external provocation is called:
questions.explanation: Radioactivity (discovered by Becquerel, 1896): spontaneous disintegration of unstable atomic nuclei with emission of radiation (α, β, γ). It is a nuclear (not chemical) process — unaffected by temperature, pressure, or chemical state.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which type of radiation has the highest penetrating power?
questions.explanation: Penetrating power: γ > β > α. Alpha particles are stopped by paper; beta by a few mm of aluminium; gamma rays need several cm of lead or metres of concrete. Ionising power is the reverse: α > β > γ.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Radioactive waste disposal is a major challenge because:

options.option_text: It can be reused as fuel immediately
Some radioactive isotopes remain dangerous for thousands of years
The waste can be easily neutralised with acid
It only emits safe infrared radiation

questions.explanation: High-level radioactive waste (spent nuclear fuel) contains long-lived isotopes like Plutonium-239 (t½=24,110 years). It must be stored in geologically stable deep repositories for tens of thousands of years.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: PET (Positron Emission Tomography) scan in medical imaging uses which type of radioactive decay?
questions.explanation: PET uses β⁺-emitting tracers (e.g., F-18 in FDG). When a positron meets an electron (annihilation), two 511 keV gamma rays are emitted in opposite directions — detected by the scanner ring to produce 3D images.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The energy released in nuclear reactions is described by Einstein's mass-energy equivalence formula:
questions.explanation: E = mc² (Einstein, 1905): energy (E) equals mass (m) × the speed of light squared (c² ≈ 9×10¹⁶ m²/s²). Even a tiny mass defect in nuclear reactions releases enormous energy.
questions.subject: Chemistry
